Priya: Quick pass on the routing editor after today's QA. Found a few UX edge cases that trip up non-engineers. Posting notes so we can prioritize. Screenshots + short Loom in thread. Tom: thanks — can you list the top 3 so we can pick wins? Priya: Top 3: 1) Visual precedence: users assume list order == priority, but the UI shows a numeric field and a drag handle. People get confused which actually controls routing. 2) Conflict resolution: when two rules share the same precedence we show an error but offer no remediation. 3) Simulator feedback: when a preview evaluates a rule, the result popover disappears on hover which makes it impossible to inspect long matches. Elena: for #1 could we hide the numeric priority unless advanced mode is toggled, and surface an inline tooltip: "Routing order is determined by list position. Edit numeric priority for explicit overrides." That reduces cognitive load. Marco: I worry hiding the number breaks power user flows. Alternative: keep number but make it read-only by default with an edit pencil. Default behavior = drag order. Edit unlocks direct numeric edits. Noor: For conflicts we could offer an auto-fix button: "Resolve now" → shift lower-priority rules down one slot and highlight changes. Must warn and allow undo. That feels less punitive than just an error. Tom: Love the auto-fix idea. We still need a clear confirmation microcopy: "This will renumber conflicting rules to preserve a single execution order. Undo available." Priya: Agreed. Keep the language calm and reversible. Also, can the simulator stop disappearing? It should stick until user clicks away or presses ESC. Right now it times out when the mouse moves a bit. Elena: Accessibility note: the simulator panel needs role=dialog and focus trap while open. Screen reader users should hear the evaluation summary and then be able to tab into details. Add aria-describedby pointing to the match summary. Marco: Quick implementation thought: simulator currently truncates examples by character count. Runtime truncates by tokenized length which changes match outcomes for long rules. Short-term patch: show a small badge "runtime may trim differently" and queue a ticket to run the same tokenizer. Long-term: call the backend preview endpoint used by runtime. Noor: Copy suggestion for saved state: ditch green check that reads as "live". Try "Saved — staging only" with a muted grey check and tooltip: "Changes are saved in drafts; deploy to apply." Priya: Also keyboard reordering: people want to move a rule quickly. Propose keyboard shortcuts when a rule is focused: Cmd/Ctrl+Up and Cmd/Ctrl+Down to move. Show a small hint on hover and in the accessible context menu. Tom: That sounds good. We'll need product + eng to agree on shortcut conflicts. I'll drop this into the RFC. Elena: Small code snippet for aria roles to share with eng:

Simulator results will appear here
Marco: Nice. Also add aria-atomic=true for the sim-results so SRs read the full update. prodbot: Created UX-4112: "Routing editor 11 precedence clarity, conflict fix UI, and simulator stickiness" — assignees: Tom, Elena; priority: P2; due: 2024-07-02. Priya: Thanks. Can we aim for a small delivery: auto-resolve button + simulator stickiness + copy tweaks for the next sprint? If yes I'll mark the tasks accordingly. Tom: Yes, I'll split UX-4112 into three sub-tasks and tag eng-runtime for tokenizer parity. Will update the ticket with comps later today. Priya: Great. I'll upload the compact/expanded comps and add the microcopy options before end of day. Thanks team!
